turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi Priya, thanks for making time. I have gone through your application and the SKU sheet. We like the creamy lick treats, but the numbers need work before we can place an order.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Thanks for having me. Happy to talk through it. What are you looking at first?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Margin. You offered 17 percent, and our treats target is 35 percent. Where can you get to?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Seventeen is thin, I know. Our tuna and salmon costs went up this year. If you take the full treats range, I can move to 21 percent.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Twenty-one is better but still short. Can you go to 24?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: No, 21 is my floor on the treats. The litter I can look at again once we see sales, but not today.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Understood, 21 percent margin is recorded. Next, payment terms. Your application says 15 days. We need at least 21 days.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Fifteen is hard for us, we are a young company. But I can do 30 days if the order is confirmed in writing this week.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Agreed, 30 days payment terms, order confirmed in writing. Now minimum order quantity. You have 800 units, and our forecast is far lower for a new brand.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: 800 is what our production batch needs. I can bring it down to 500 units in total for the first order, split across the SKUs you list.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Good, 500 units in total for the first order, split across the SKUs we list. What about launch marketing support? You listed 20,000 rupees.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: We can raise that to 50,000 rupees for the launch month, to be used on sponsored listings and sampling.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thank you. And a launch discount for the first month? Your application has none.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: I can give a 5 percent launch discount for the first 30 days.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That works. One more request: sale-or-return on unsold stock after 90 days, since this is a new brand for us.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: I am sorry, I cannot accept returns of unsold stock. Treats have a short shelf life and we cannot resell them. Defect returns within 7 days stay as they are.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Fine, no sale-or-return. Before we recap, one thing on the cat litter: you said you would look at it again. Can you offer something now?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: For the litter I can do a base margin of 15 percent. On top of that I will give you 20 percent marketing support on sales if you sell 2,000 units across the range within the first 90 days.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: 2,000 units in 90 days is far above what we expect for a new brand, and 15 percent is well under our litter target. Can the margin be guaranteed instead of depending on volume?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: The volume target is how I fund the marketing. The 15 percent base stays guaranteed, and the 20 percent applies only if you reach 2,000 units.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Understood, we will evaluate that structure separately. To recap: 21 percent margin, 30 days payment, 500 units MOQ, 50,000 rupees marketing support, 5 percent launch discount for 30 days, defect returns within 7 days only.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: That is correct. I will send the written confirmation by Friday.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi Priya, thanks for making time. I have gone through your application and the SKU sheet. We like the creamy lick treats, but the numbers need work before we can place an order.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Thanks for having me. Happy to talk through it. What are you looking at first?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Margin. You offered 17 percent, and our treats target is 35 percent. Where can you get to?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Seventeen is thin, I know. Our tuna and salmon costs went up this year. If you take the full treats range, I can move to 21 percent.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Twenty-one is better but still short. Can you go to 24?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: No, 21 is my floor on the treats. The litter I can look at again once we see sales, but not today.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Understood, 21 percent margin is recorded. Next, payment terms. Your application says 15 days. We need at least 21 days.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: Fifteen is hard for us, we are a young company. But I can do 30 days if the order is confirmed in writing this week.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Agreed, 30 days payment terms, order confirmed in writing. Now minimum order quantity. You have 800 units, and our forecast is far lower for a new brand.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: 800 is what our production batch needs. I can bring it down to 500 units in total for the first order, split across the SKUs you list.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Good, 500 units in total for the first order, split across the SKUs we list. What about launch marketing support? You listed 20,000 rupees.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: We can raise that to 50,000 rupees for the launch month, to be used on sponsored listings and sampling.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thank you. And a launch discount for the first month? Your application has none.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: I can give a 5 percent launch discount for the first 30 days.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That works. One more request: sale-or-return on unsold stock after 90 days, since this is a new brand for us.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: I am sorry, I cannot accept returns of unsold stock. Treats have a short shelf life and we cannot resell them. Defect returns within 7 days stay as they are.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Fine, no sale-or-return. Before we recap, one thing on the cat litter: you said you would look at it again. Can you offer something now?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: For the litter I can do a base margin of 15 percent. On top of that I will give you 20 percent marketing support on sales if you sell 2,000 units across the range within the first 90 days.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: 2,000 units in 90 days is far above what we expect for a new brand, and 15 percent is well under our litter target. Can the margin be guaranteed instead of depending on volume?

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: The volume target is how I fund the marketing. The 15 percent base stays guaranteed, and the 20 percent applies only if you reach 2,000 units.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Understood, we will evaluate that structure separately. To recap: 21 percent margin, 30 days payment, 500 units MOQ, 50,000 rupees marketing support, 5 percent launch discount for 30 days, defect returns within 7 days only.

turns.speaker: vendor
turns.text: That is correct. I will send the written confirmation by Friday.
